sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

items.prompt: A bag has 2 red and 3 blue marbles. What is the theoretical probability of drawing red?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

items.prompt: A fair coin is flipped and a 3-section spinner is spun. What is the probability of heads and landing on section 2?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: A outfit is made by choosing one shirt color from 4 options and one shorts color from 3 options. How many different outfits are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 5-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 27 times in 135 spins. A simulation of 135 spins landed on that section 29 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 0. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 30 times and landed on blue 8 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A bag has 2 red, 4 blue, and 9 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 6 equal sections numbered 1 to 6 is spun. What is the probability of getting heads on the coin and landing on 2 on the spinner?
A pizza is made by choosing one topping from 5 options and one crust from 3 options. How many different pizzas are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 8-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 33 times in 264 spins. A simulation of 264 spins landed on that section 39 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
